name: @spiritsurge/figma-mcp

tools.name: clone_node
tools.description: Duplicate a node with all its children, styles and effects intact, optionally at a new position. Returns the copy's subtree and its pageId — the copies have new ids. Pass parent_id to put the copy on another page or in another frame; the original is untouched. Use this rather than rebuilding a design from its parts. This modifies the document.

depth.description:
Levels of the copy's subtree to return. Defaults to 2, which is enough
to address the copy's direct children.

name.description: Layer name for the copy. Defaults to Figma's own "name (Copy)".

parent_id.description:
Page or frame to put the copy in, so it can land on another page. Omit
to keep it beside the original. Position is kept relative to the new
parent unless `x`/`y` are given.

x.description: Where to put the copy. Omit either to leave it on top of the original.

tools.name: create_image
tools.description: Place an image file from this machine onto the current Figma page as a new layer. This modifies the document.

name.description: Layer name. Defaults to the file's own name.

path.description: Absolute path to a PNG or JPEG on this machine.

width.description: Displayed size. Defaults to the image's own pixel dimensions.

x.description: Position on the current page, in Figma canvas coordinates.

tools.name: create_page
tools.description: Add a page to the file and return its id. Does not switch to it. Put nodes on it with clone_node and parent_id. This modifies the document.

index.description: Position among the pages, from 0. Defaults to the end.

name.description: Name for the new page. Refused if a page already has this name.

tools.name: delete_nodes
tools.description: Delete nodes by id. Ids that no longer exist are reported rather than failing the call. This modifies the document.

tools.name: delete_page
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE: permanently delete one page and every layer on it from the open file. One page id only, no patterns. Refused for the page the user has open, for the last page in the file, and for anything that is not a page. Returns the deleted page's name and how many layers it held. Confirm with the user before calling. Figma's undo may recover it, but do not rely on that.

page_id.description: The page to delete, as returned by get_pages or create_page.

tools.name: export_svg
tools.description: Export a node as SVG, so icons and logos stay vector. The file is saved to disk and its path returned; small SVGs are also returned inline.

node_id.description: Node to export, e.g. an icon or logo frame.

outline_text.description:
Convert text to outlines so the SVG renders without the font. Defaults
to true; set false to keep text as live `<text>`.

tools.name: find_nodes
tools.description: Find nodes by type, name, solid fill or stroke colour, style id, variable id or component, and count how many there are. Returns ids and layer paths, not subtrees; read an id with get_node. At least one filter is required. This is also the usage lookup: filter by style_id, variable_id or component_id to see where one is used, with limit 0 for just the count. Searches inside instances too, so overrides are found. Text with mixed styles matches only on its node-level style.

all_pages.description: Search every page. Slow on a large file. Ignored when `root_id` is set.

component_id.description: Instances of this component, or of any variant in this component set.

fill_color.description: A solid fill colour as #rrggbb. Alpha is ignored.

limit.description:
Most matches to return; the total is always counted in full. Default
200. Use 0 to count uses without listing them.

name.description: Layer name contains this text, ignoring case.

root_id.description:
Search under this node (a page id works). Omit to search the current
page; set `all_pages` to search the whole file.

stroke_color.description: A solid stroke colour as #rrggbb. Alpha is ignored.

style_id.description: A fill, stroke, text or effect style id, as returned by get_styles.

types.description: Keep only these node types, e.g. ["INSTANCE", "TEXT", "RECTANGLE"].

variable_id.description:
A variable id bound to any field, fill, stroke or effect, as returned
by get_variable_defs or by `variableId` on a fill in get_node.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Read the structure of the open Figma document as a node tree. Prefer a depth limit or get_node on a specific frame; a whole large file can be tens of megabytes.

depth.description:
How many levels of the node tree to include. Omit for the whole tree,
which on a large file can be very large indeed.

tools.name: get_image_bytes
tools.description: Read the original bytes of an image fill by its hash (imageHash in get_node). The file is saved to disk and its path returned, in the format it was uploaded in.

hash.description: An image hash, as `imageHash` on an IMAGE fill in get_node.

tools.name: get_metadata
tools.description: Read file name, current page and selection count. Cheap; useful as a first call to confirm which file is open.

tools.name: get_node
tools.description: Read one node and its subtree by id. This is the right tool for inspecting a specific frame or component.

node_id.description: Figma node id, as it appears in a file URL, e.g. "1:23".

tools.name: get_pages
tools.description: List the pages in the open document.

tools.name: get_screenshot
tools.description: Render a node or the current page to a base64 PNG. Use when the visual result matters more than the structure.

node_id.description: Node to render. Omit to render the current page.

scale.description: Render scale; 1.0 is the design's own size. Defaults to 2.0.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Read the nodes the user currently has selected in Figma. Use this when the user refers to 'this' or 'the selected frame'.

tools.name: get_styles
tools.description: Read the document's local paint, text, effect and grid styles — the design system's named values.

tools.name: get_variable_defs
tools.description: Read the document's variable collections and their values across modes — design tokens, in Figma's terms.

tools.name: set_text
tools.description: Replace the contents of a text node, keeping its font, size, colour and effects. Returns the previous text and the node's new size. This modifies the document.

characters.description: The new contents. May be empty.

instructions:
Reads the Figma document currently open in the desktop or web app, through a plugin the user runs and connects.

If a tool reports that no plugin is connected, tell the user to open the plugin in Figma and select this session — it is not something you can fix by retrying.

Start with get_metadata to confirm which file is open. Prefer get_selection or get_node over get_document: whole-document reads on a real file are very large.
